open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure boundary for direct service access
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them” and A07’s “no agent ever holds it” conflict with “An agent's own access to a service — as for processing a photo — is granted by that service and the owner outside the kernel; ... its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Is the prohibition on agents receiving personal data global, or does it apply only to values returned through the kernel surface, allowing direct service access to reveal personal data?
options: The prohibition applies only to kernel responses; service-granted direct access may reveal personal data
The prohibition is global; direct service access must also return only digest and class
Direct access is allowed only to service data not classified as personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as a kernel-surface guarantee only and leave direct-service disclosure to the service and owner.

open_points.subject: return path for a photo processed directly by an agent
open_points.text: “the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel, with its own access to the service that holds the photo rather than through the kernel, and the kernel moves the file between services” while K-10 says “a caller never hands the kernel a file.”
open_points.question: After the agent obtains and processes the photo, through what named service operation or capability do the resulting bytes return to service custody so an operation node can move them through the kernel?
options: The agent writes the processed file back through a direct API of the source service
The agent writes it to another service that exposes it to an operation node
The agent only analyzes the photo and produces value metadata; no processed file re-enters the flow
open_points.default_guess: The agent writes the processed file back to the source service using owner-granted direct service access, after which a flow operation reads it.

open_points.subject: reverse-proxy-only access to the kernel listener
open_points.text: “The proxy terminates TLS and is the only client of the kernel's listener, whose address the installation names and which the host does not expose otherwise.”
open_points.question: Which named owner or capability configures and verifies that the listener is not externally exposed and that only the TLS-terminating reverse proxy can connect to it?
options: A host deployment procedure outside the kernel owns and verifies it
`surface.serve_kernel` enforces authenticated or encrypted proxy-to-kernel transport
open_points.default_guess: Treat this as a host deployment invariant owned outside the kernel, with no runtime verification by the kernel.
